scope: Home electricity, cooking gas, and travel by road, rail and air. Direct emissions only.

factors.label: Grid electricity
factors.source: Central Electricity Authority (India), CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector, User Guide v20.0, December 2024, Table S: all-India weighted average, FY 2023-24 (adjusted for cross-border transfers, including renewables)
factors.note: CO2 only, per unit generated. Transmission and distribution losses are not added.

factors.label: Cooking gas (LPG)
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Fuels": LPG, 2,939.4 kg CO2e per tonne
factors.note: Counted per 14.2 kg cylinder, the standard domestic size in India.

factors.label: Car (petrol)
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Passenger vehicles": average car, petrol
factors.note: Per vehicle-km, not divided among passengers. UK fleet average; Indian cars are typically smaller.

factors.label: Car (diesel)
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Passenger vehicles": average car, diesel
factors.note: Per vehicle-km, not divided among passengers.

factors.label: Motorbike or scooter
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Passenger vehicles": motorbike, average (petrol)

factors.label: Taxi or cab
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Business travel- land": regular taxi
factors.note: Also the closest available figure for app cabs. No separate auto-rickshaw factor could be sourced.

factors.label: Bus
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Business travel- land": average local bus
factors.note: At UK passenger loads. Fuller Indian buses emit less per passenger, so this tends to overstate.

factors.label: Train or metro
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Business travel- land": national rail
factors.note: Low confidence. This reflects the UK rail and grid mix, which differ a lot from India. Treat as a rough guide.

factors.label: Flight within India
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Business travel- air": short-haul, average passenger, without radiative forcing
factors.note: Indian domestic flights are closer in length to short-haul than to UK domestic flights. Excludes radiative forcing (contrails and high-altitude effects), which can raise aviation impact substantially.

factors.label: International flight
factors.source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero, Greenhouse gas reporting: conversion factors 2026 (full set), sheet "Business travel- air": international, to/from non-UK, average passenger, without radiative forcing

india.label: India, average per person
india.source: Global Carbon Budget (2025) via Our World in Data, "CO2 emissions per capita": fossil fuels and industry, all sectors, excluding land use. Retrieved 2026-10-18.

world.label: World, average per person
world.source: Global Carbon Budget (2025) via Our World in Data, "CO2 emissions per capita": fossil fuels and industry, all sectors, excluding land use. Retrieved 2026-10-18.

exclusions: Food and diet: no India-specific factors could be sourced to a standard we would stand behind.
Upstream fuel supply (extraction, refining, vehicle manufacture).
Radiative forcing from flights (contrails and high-altitude effects).
caveats: This is an estimate from the figures you enter, not an audited inventory.
Vehicle, bus, rail and flight factors come from UK government data. Indian fleets and loads differ, so treat those lines as approximate; each carries a confidence tag.
The national averages are totals across all sectors, including industry. Your figure covers home energy and travel only, so the comparison is for scale, not a like-for-like score.
Trees take years to reach the absorption rates shown. Comparing your footprint with your trees is a reality check, not an offset.
Your footprint never affects your credits or rewards.
